evidence.claim: Big Cottonwood Canyon Scenic Byway heads east on SR-190 from the canyon mouth, with the walls closing in almost immediately.
evidence.quote: The byway begins at the mouth of the canyon and goes east on S.R. 190. The canyon narrows almost immediately to dramatic alpine scenery as you enter the forest.

evidence.claim: Visit Utah lists this state scenic byway as a 15-mile, 25-minute drive and highlights its alpine scenery, old mining country and recreation.
evidence.quote: Big Cottonwood Canyon Scenic Byway 15 miles | 25 minutes

evidence.claim: Trailheads, picnic areas, cabins and historic water and mining works line the canyon route.
evidence.quote: The route passes many trailheads and picnic areas within the canyon, as well as historic water- and mining-related infrastructure and a few areas of cabins, before passing Solitude Mountain Resort and looping through Brighton.

evidence.claim: The highway developed in stages: part of the present route entered the state system in 1933 as SR-152, reaching the national forest boundary.
evidence.quote: The first piece of present SR-190 was added to the state highway system in 1933 as part of Utah State Route 152 (SR-152), which followed Highland Drive, 6200 South, and Big Cottonwood Canyon Road from Salt Lake City to the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest boundary in Big Cottonwood Canyon.

evidence.claim: That designation extended to Brighton in 1941.
evidence.quote: In 1941, SR-152 was extended east in the forest to Brighton

evidence.claim: In 1963, an extension followed an existing county road over Guardsman Pass to provide access to the new Wasatch Mountain State Park.
evidence.quote: In order to provide access to the new Wasatch Mountain State Park, SR-152 was extended east from Brighton in 1963, following an existing county road over Guardsman Pass to end at SR-224.

evidence.claim: The canyon section became SR-190 in 1987.
evidence.quote: in 1987, a piece in the middle of SR-152

evidence.claim: From the canyon mouth, the drive passes Stairs Station, a hydroelectric plant built in 1894–1895, before reaching Solitude and the loop through Brighton.
evidence.quote: before passing Solitude Mountain Resort and looping through Brighton.

evidence.claim: The Forest Service identifies Silver Lake and its visitor center among the destinations reached by the drive.
evidence.quote: The road leads tot two four-season ski resorts and the popular Silver Lake and Silver Lake Visitor Center.

evidence.claim: For a summer continuation toward Park City, the connection to Guardsman Pass requires some backtracking from the Brighton loop and follows a narrower mountain road.
evidence.quote: After looping through Brighton, the route connects (with some backtracking) to a narrower mountain road across Guardsman Pass

evidence.claim: That crossing normally closes all winter.
evidence.quote: This part of the road is normally closed all winter.

evidence.claim: Stairs Station was built in 1894–1895 to generate hydroelectric power.
evidence.quote: The Stairs Station Hydroelectric Power Plant was built in 1894-1895 in Big Cottonwood Canyon

evidence.claim: Robert M. Jones designed the station for his Big Cottonwood Power Company, which contracted in 1895 to supply the Salt Lake and Ogden Gas and Electric Company.
evidence.quote: The station was designed by Robert M. Jones for his Big Cottonwood Power Company at a cost of $325,000. In 1895 the company contracted to provide power to the Salt Lake and Ogden Gas and Electric Company

evidence.claim: Its two-story powerhouse placed generating equipment below and switchgear above.
evidence.quote: The station was designed in the Second Renaissance Revival style with two levels, the lower housing the generating equipment, the upper formerly housing switchgear.

evidence.claim: Four original Pelton wheels have given way to one Francis turbine.
evidence.quote: The power plant was originally built with four Pelton wheels, since replaced by a single Francis turbine

evidence.claim: The powerhouse is the plant’s only remaining building, part of a system that also includes penstocks and a pipeline.
evidence.quote: The plant comprises the powerhouse, switchyard, penstocks, and a pipeline.

evidence.claim: Its Second Renaissance Revival design gives this industrial site an architectural identity of its own.
evidence.quote: The station was designed in the Second Renaissance Revival style

evidence.claim: The powerhouse is the plant’s only remaining building
evidence.quote: The powerhouse is the only remaining building associated with the plant.

evidence.claim: Doughnut Falls drops into a pothole in the rock, with an arch above the pool.
evidence.quote: The waterfall plunges into a pothole that has access under the arch of rock with a view up at the falls falling into the pool.

evidence.claim: The waterfall lies near Silver Fork in Big Cottonwood Canyon, reached from the Mill D Trailhead toward the Jordan Pines picnic area.
evidence.quote: Doughnut Falls (also known as Donut Falls) is a waterfall in the Big Cottonwood Canyon near Silver Fork, south of Midvale in Salt Lake County, Utah. Access to Doughnut Falls is from the Mill D Trailhead towards the Jordan Pines picnic area.

evidence.claim: The summer hike is about 1.5 miles round trip if parking is available; a different winter approach can take up to 3.5 miles round trip.
evidence.quote: In the winter, you need to take an alternative path to reach the often frozen waterfall, which can take up to 3.5 miles round trip, but in Summer the hike is about 1.5 miles long round trip, if you can find a parking spot.

evidence.claim: An old elevator motor helped launch Brighton’s ski area.
evidence.quote: Brighton was started in 1936 when members of the Alpine Ski Club built a rope tow from wire and an old elevator motor.

evidence.claim: In 1936, Alpine Ski Club members combined it with wire to build a rope tow, beginning what became Utah’s first ski resort.
evidence.quote: Brighton Ski Resort was the first ski resort in Utah, and one of the first in the United States. Brighton was started in 1936 when members of the Alpine Ski Club built a rope tow from wire and an old elevator motor.

evidence.claim: The town occupies the top of Big Cottonwood Canyon and includes both Brighton and Solitude ski resorts.
evidence.quote: Brighton is located at the top of Big Cottonwood Canyon

evidence.claim: Its municipal story is much newer than its skiing: residents voted to incorporate in November 2018, and incorporation took effect on January 1, 2020.
evidence.quote: On November 6, 2018, residents of the area voted for incorporation, which took effect January 1, 2020.

evidence.claim: SR-190 makes a loop through Brighton before connecting, with backtracking, to the Guardsman Pass road.
evidence.quote: After looping through Brighton, the route connects (with some backtracking) to a narrower mountain road across Guardsman Pass

evidence.claim: includes both Brighton and Solitude ski resorts
evidence.quote: Both the Brighton Ski Resort and the Solitude Mountain Resort are located in Brighton.

evidence.claim: Big Cottonwood Creek formed the V-shaped canyon, with its many rock formations.
evidence.quote: Since the canyon was formed by Big Cottonwood Creek, the V-shaped canyon has many impressive rock forms.

evidence.claim: The area was first settled in 1871.
evidence.quote: The area was first settled in 1871 but remained unincorporated.
